title: Rice Pudding
subtitle: Baked creamy pudding rice with vanilla and a golden skin
excerpt: Short-grain pudding rice baked very slowly in a sweetened vanilla custard until each grain is swollen and tender and the top has set into a golden-brown skin. Comfort food in its simplest form.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rice pudding is one of the oldest desserts in British cooking, appearing in cookbooks as far back as the fifteenth century. The dish is part of a broader international family of sweet rice preparations: arroz con leche in Spain and Latin America, riz au lait in France, risengrod in Scandinavia, and kheer across South and Central Asia. All share the same basic principle of rice cooked slowly in sweetened milk until thick and creamy. The British version is traditionally baked in the oven in a shallow dish, which produces the characteristic browned skin on the surface. The skin is considered a delicacy by those who grew up with the dish and is the first thing eaten when the pudding comes out of the oven. The rice used is a short-grain pudding rice, not long-grain or basmati: short-grain rice releases starch as it absorbs the milk, producing the thick, creamy consistency of a good pudding.

recipeTools.notes: A shallow baking dish, approximately 1.5 litre capacity.

content.text: The pudding requires a very low oven and a long cooking time: high heat causes the milk to curdle and the pudding to set unevenly. It should not be stirred during baking once the skin has begun to form. If the skin colours too quickly, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the dish. The pudding is done when it has a thick, browned skin on top and the rice inside is completely tender and swimming in a creamy, lightly set sauce. It firms up considerably on cooling.

Heat the oven to 140 C / fan 120 C / gas 1. Put the rice in a buttered baking dish. Add the milk, cream, sugar, and vanilla and stir to combine. Dot with small pieces of butter. Grate nutmeg generously over the surface.

Bake for 30 minutes, then stir the skin gently back into the pudding. Bake for a further 90 minutes without stirring, until the rice is completely tender and a golden-brown skin has formed on top. Serve hot from the dish with jam alongside if you like.
